paragraphs.title: The Fall of the Idols and God's Carrying of Israel

easy.explanation: The passage begins, “Bel boweth down, Nebo stoopeth.”
easy.q: Who boweth down at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: The idols were upon the beasts and cattle as a heavy load.
easy.q: Upon whom were the idols placed as a heavy burden?

easy.explanation: God says, “I will carry you, and will deliver you.”
easy.q: Whom does God promise to carry and deliver?

answers: The idols are carried, but God carries Israel
The idols save, but God falls
The idols speak, but God is silent
medium.explanation: The idols become burdens, while God carries and delivers His people.
medium.q: What is the main contrast between the idols and God?

answers: They become a burden and go into captivity
medium.explanation: They cannot deliver the burden and are themselves taken into captivity.
medium.q: What happens to the idols after they bow down?

answers: He has cared for Israel from the beginning of its life
He brought Israel from the east
medium.explanation: God says Israel has been borne by Him from the belly and carried from the womb.
medium.q: What does “from the belly” suggest about God's care for Israel?

challenge.explanation: Their captivity shows that they are powerless and unable to deliver themselves.
challenge.q: What does the idols' going into captivity show about them?

answers: His care will continue throughout Israel's life
The idols will become stronger in old age
challenge.explanation: God promises to carry Israel even to old age and hoar hairs.
challenge.q: What does God promise by saying, “even to your old age”?

answers: The idols move by their own power
The idols need to be carried, while God carries and delivers
challenge.explanation: The idols depend on others for movement, but God carries His people and saves them.
challenge.q: Why does calling the idols a burden emphasize God's superiority?

easy.explanation: The passage asks, “To whom will ye liken me?” and then describes an idol made by men.
easy.q: To whom does God ask whether He should be likened?

easy.explanation: They lavish gold out of the bag, weigh silver, and hire a goldsmith.
easy.q: What do the worshipers give to the goldsmith?

easy.explanation: The people fall down and worship the image.
easy.q: What do the people do after the god is made?

answers: The idol answers, moves, and is then made
The people pay, the image is made, and they carry and set it down
The people pray, the idol saves, and silver is weighed
medium.explanation: The worshipers provide the precious metal, the goldsmith makes the idol, and the people carry and place it.
medium.q: What sequence of actions is described in the passage?

answers: Pay a craftsman to make the idol
Return the idol to its owner
medium.explanation: The people pay a goldsmith to make the image into a god.
medium.q: What does “hire a goldsmith” mean in this passage?

answers: It rescues the people carrying it
medium.explanation: The image must be carried and placed because it cannot move on its own.
medium.q: Why does carrying the image and setting it in place show its weakness?

answers: The idol answers and saves him
The idol moves to help him
The idol cannot answer or save him
challenge.explanation: The passage says the idol cannot answer or save him out of his trouble.
challenge.q: What happens when someone cries to the idol in trouble?

answers: The people carry, place, and worship it, while it does nothing
The people do nothing, while the idol makes itself
The people seek help, while the idol saves them
challenge.explanation: All the actions are performed by the people; the idol remains motionless and powerless.
challenge.q: What difference is shown between the worshipers and the idol?

answers: They show an image made, carried, and dependent on people
They show an image that knows the future
They describe an image that saves in trouble
challenge.explanation: The idol is a human-made object that cannot move, answer, or save.
challenge.q: How do these verses challenge the idea that God can be compared with an idol?

answers: Remember and bring the matter to mind
easy.explanation: They are told to remember and bring the former things again to mind.
easy.q: What are the transgressors told to do?

answers: There are many gods like Him
He is God, and there is none like Him
easy.explanation: God declares, “I am God, and there is none like me.”
easy.q: What does God say about His uniqueness?

easy.explanation: God declares the end from the beginning and things not yet done.

answers: God knows the future but does not act
God declares what will happen and brings His counsel to pass
medium.explanation: God declares the end and says, “My counsel shall stand.”
medium.q: What connection is made between God's knowledge of the future and His counsel?

medium.explanation: The man from the east refers to Cyrus, whom God used to execute His counsel.
medium.q: Who is the man called from the east in this passage?

answers: God fulfills what He has declared
medium.explanation: God says that what He has spoken He will also bring to pass.
medium.q: What does the sequence “I have spoken it... I will also bring it to pass” teach?

answers: It directs the people to consider God's works in the past
It describes how idols were made
challenge.explanation: Remembering God's former works helps the people recognize His uniqueness and faithfulness.
challenge.q: Why is the command to remember “the former things of old” important?

answers: The man demonstrates that God directs the fulfillment of His counsel
challenge.explanation: God calls the man from the east to carry out the purpose God has declared.
challenge.q: What relationship is shown between the one true God and the man from the east?

answers: God's counsel shall stand and His pleasure will be done
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that God's counsel stands and that He will do all His pleasure.
challenge.q: What conclusion follows from the repeated statements about God's purpose?

paragraphs.title: The Promise of Righteousness and Salvation

answers: The stouthearted who are far from righteousness
easy.explanation: God addresses those who are stouthearted and far from righteousness.
easy.q: To whom does God speak at the beginning of this passage?

easy.explanation: God says, “I bring near my righteousness.”
God promises, “I will place salvation in Zion.”

medium.explanation: God declares that His salvation “shall not tarry.”
medium.q: What does God promise about the timing of salvation?

medium.explanation: God brings His righteousness near and says that His salvation will not be far off.
medium.q: What relationship is shown between righteousness and salvation?

medium.explanation: The passage ends with the words, “For Israel my glory.”
medium.q: What will Israel be according to the closing words?

answers: People who are hard-hearted and far from righteousness
People who have already been saved
challenge.explanation: The stouthearted are addressed as those who are far from righteousness.
challenge.q: What does the description “stouthearted” suggest in this context?

answers: It shows that God's promise will be fulfilled in salvation
It makes people the rulers of everything
challenge.explanation: As God's counsel stands, so His righteousness and salvation will come to pass.
challenge.q: How does this passage connect with the earlier teaching about God's purpose?

answers: Righteousness and salvation are brought near
challenge.explanation: God declares that His righteousness is near and His salvation will not be delayed.
challenge.q: What change does the passage present for those who are far from righteousness?
